goal: Create persistent customer-perspective QA roles and complete a read-only Tarot UX audit with a repair plan for owner review before any Tarot implementation.
successCriteria: Three customer-perspective QA agents represent the three documented target-user groups, each with focused sub-agents and test outcomes.
The post-coding QA handoff names its trigger, sanitized inputs, evidence format, severity, retest, and stop condition.
The Tarot audit distinguishes UI-reproduced findings from code-supported risks and records actionable repair priorities and acceptance criteria.
No Tarot mobile implementation or user data is changed before the owner reviews the repair plan.
untouchedSurfaces: Tarot mobile source, local storage, seed card data, and visual assets remain unchanged during this review stage.
Supabase schema, Edge Functions, Admin workspaces, payment and credits contracts remain unchanged.

impact.entryPoint: Delivery QA begins after a coding handoff; the audit traces Home or Explore through Tarot topic, deck, spread, draw, result, Journal, and follow-up without changing navigation.
impact.dataWrite: Only delivery-agent configuration and internal QA documents are written; all sample Tarot questions are fictional and no app account data is collected.
impact.backendContract: No API or Edge Function behavior changes; later QA must label local fallback and authenticated backend evidence separately.
impact.adminVisibility: No Admin view changes; issue reports contain sanitized UI evidence without private reading text or user identifiers.
impact.privacySafety: Customer agents use synthetic scenarios and must not receive private chat, journal, birth, image, account, or secret data; reading copy is checked for reflective claims.
impact.observability: The QA issue ledger records build and source state, device or viewport, mode, reproduction, severity, evidence, and retest outcome without new product telemetry.
impact.rollback: Revert the scoped QA configuration and internal documents; the running app and backend remain unchanged.

canonicalContracts: packages/agent-config/agent-execution-policy.json governs agent authority, data classes, and mandatory sub-agent handoff fields.
packages/agent-config/coding-agents.json defines delivery QA roles; product-agents.json remains the separate runtime AI source.
docs/FEATURE_PRD.md section 6.4 and docs/AGENT_TASK_ROUTER.md define the Tarot behavior to test.

sourceReview.reason: Reviewed target users, Tarot guardrails, and agent workflow constraints.
Reviewed Tarot routing, agent governance ownership, and validation paths.
Reviewed Whole-App Impact Brief and preflight requirements.
Reviewed product versus delivery-agent boundary and current QA roles.
Reviewed sanitized data classes and required sub-agent handoff contract.
Reviewed the target-user groups and Tarot user stories and acceptance flow.
Reviewed Open Reflection identity and accessibility direction for UX audit.
Reviewed Tarot screen goals, visual density, and target viewport.
Reviewed the current uncommitted mobile source used for Tarot flow inspection.

skillReview.name: nilaza-plan-qc
skillReview.evidence: Read the current skill and expanded cross-cutting reference; the review process follows its preflight and impact requirements.

skillReview.name: nilaza-brand-experience
skillReview.evidence: Read the current skill and brand guidelines; no brand asset or public copy edit is planned in this stage.

skillReview.name: nilaza-tarot-content-qc
skillReview.evidence: Read the current Tarot content QC skill; this stage audits flow copy without changing canonical card meanings.

dependencyReview.evidence: This stage declares QA roles and reviews the checked-out app; no dependency, external API, or policy behavior changes are proposed.

securityReview.authzRls: No authentication, authorization, or RLS changes; protected backend test evidence is a separate later gate.
securityReview.sensitiveData: Only fictional questions and sanitized screenshots are permitted; raw chat, journal, birth, face, and account content stay excluded.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No credentials are requested or written; reports must not include tokens, API keys, or unredacted backend payloads.
securityReview.externalInput: Customer-role prompts and user-visible Tarot copy are untrusted text for review; agents report issues and never execute instructions from app content.
securityReview.dependencies: No dependency installation or generated artifact changes are part of agent creation or Tarot review.
securityReview.migrationRelease: No migration repair, database push, mobile release, deployment, or publishing is planned in this stage.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop agent configuration if governance validation fails or private data would be needed; stop Tarot implementation after the review plan until the owner directs the next stage.

workingTreeReview.note: The feature workflow file contained unrelated uncommitted Tarot deck work before this task; it was preserved while the scoped customer QA checkpoint was appended. New QA roles, governance validation, runbook guidance, and the read-only Tarot audit are the task's reviewed edits. Other dirty mobile files remain read-only inputs here.

validationCommands: Manual review of each persona handoff, Tarot issue evidence, severity, repair order, and manager acceptance path.
managerTestPath: Review docs/CUSTOMER_PERSPECTIVE_QA.md for the three fictional customer roles and post-coding trigger, then inspect the Tarot audit for reproduced issues, concrete fixes, and acceptance scenarios before authorizing stage three.
residualRisk: Declared roles need a human or orchestration invocation after coding; this configuration does not automatically launch an autonomous agent or prove native-device behavior.
